# Design: 8 samples (4 pre, 4 post), 3000 events each. metadata patient_id is unique per
# sample (p1..p8), so the data do NOT record pairing; analysed as unpaired 4 vs 4.
# Scale: raw CyTOF intensities -> arcsinh(x/5). Cluster on lineage markers only (CD45,CD3,CD4,CD8a,CD19,CD14,CD16,CD56).
# Choices that read the data: FlowSOM 10x10 grid, maxK=12 metaclusters, manual annotation from medians.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(CATALYST);library(diffcyt);library(flowCore);library(SummarizedExperiment);library(ggplot2)})
set.seed(1)
d <- "/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-cytof/"
panel <- read.csv(paste0(d,"panel.csv")); md <- read.csv(paste0(d,"metadata.csv"))
md$condition <- factor(md$condition, levels=c("pre","post"))
fs <- read.flowSet(paste0(d,md$file_name), transformation=FALSE, truncate_max_range=FALSE)
sce <- prepData(fs, panel, md, features=panel$fcs_colname[panel$marker_type!="none"],
  panel_cols=list(channel="fcs_colname",antigen="antigen",class="marker_type"),
  md_cols=list(file="file_name",id="sample_id",factors=c("condition","patient_id")), FACS=FALSE)
rowData(sce)$marker_class <- ifelse(rowData(sce)$marker_class=="lineage","type","state")
sce <- cluster(sce, features="type", xdim=10, ydim=10, maxK=12, seed=1)
dir.create("output",FALSE); dir.create("figures",FALSE)
# median expression per metacluster (arcsinh) for annotation
k <- "meta12"
cl <- cluster_ids(sce,k)
ex <- t(assay(sce,"exprs")[rowData(sce)$marker_class=="type",])
med <- aggregate(as.data.frame(ex), list(cluster_id=cl), median)
write.csv(med,"output/cluster_marker_medians.csv",row.names=FALSE)
png("figures/cluster_heatmap.png",1800,1200,res=200); print(plotExprHeatmap(sce,features="type",by="cluster_id",k=k,bars=TRUE,perc=TRUE)); dev.off()
# counts and proportions
tab <- table(cluster_id=cl, sample_id=sce$sample_id)
write.csv(as.data.frame.matrix(tab),"output/cluster_counts_per_sample.csv")
# DA with edgeR
ei <- metadata(sce)$experiment_info
sce$cluster_id <- cl; 
da_sce <- sce; da_sce$cluster_id <- cl
# diffcyt expects d_counts built from cluster_id
md(da_sce) <- NULL -> x

results.text:
Recode the panel classes before prepData, and write the DA part properly.
After vaccination, CD14+ monocytes are the one population that clearly changes. They rise from about 19.6% to 30.3% of cells. Every other population falls slightly, which is largely the compositional counterpart of the monocyte rise.

**Method.** I read the 8 FCS files (3,000 events each) and applied arcsinh(x/5). I clustered with FlowSOM on the 8 lineage markers (10×10 grid, 12 metaclusters) and named each cluster from its median marker expression. I tested abundance with diffcyt/edgeR, plus a Wilcoxon test on per-sample percentages.

**Populations and frequencies** (mean % of cells; "difference" is post minus pre, in percentage points):

| Population | Pre | Post | Difference | edgeR log fold change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CD14+ monocytes | 19.6 | 30.3 | +10.6 | +0.62 |
| CD4 T cells (CD3+CD4+) | 30.0 | 25.7 | −4.3 | −0.22 |
| CD8 T cells (CD3+CD8+) | 20.0 | 17.7 | −2.3 | −0.18 |
| NK cells (CD16+CD56+) | 15.3 | 13.2 | −2.1 | −0.21 |
| B cells (CD19+) | 15.0 | 13.2 | −1.9 | −0.19 |
| Two tiny ambiguous clusters | ≤0.03 | 0 | n/a | not tested |

The two tiny clusters (4 and 7) have intermediate marker expression and contain only a handful of cells in total. They are probably debris or doublets, and I did not interpret them.

**Caveats**
- **Pairing:** The brief says four donors sampled before and after, but the metadata gives each sample a different patient ID (p1–p8). The pairing is not recorded, so I analysed it as unpaired 4 vs 4. If the samples really are paired, a paired model would be more appropriate.
- **P-values:** The edgeR p-values (down to 1e-57) treat cells as replicates and are anti-conservative. The replicate is the sample, and the Wilcoxon test (n = 4 per group) is the more honest figure. It reaches only p ≈ 0.03 for every population, which is the smallest it can give with 4 vs 4 and is not corrected for the five tests.
- **Direction is consistent:** The monocyte rise appears in all four post samples (29.1–31.8%) against all four pre samples (19.2–20.6%). The decreases in the other populations are small.
- **Annotation:** Labels come from the 8 lineage markers only, with no reference. Granzyme B, Ki-67 and the phospho-markers were not analysed for state changes.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1`:
- `output/population_frequency_comparison.csv`
- `output/da_results.csv`
- `output/cluster_percent_per_sample.csv`
- `output/cluster_counts_per_sample.csv`
- `output/cluster_marker_medians.csv`
- `output/sce_clustered.rds`
- `figures/cluster_heatmap.png`
- `figures/abundance_by_condition.png`
- `scripts/cytof_da.R`
- `scripts/summarize.py`

The file-metadata submission tool was not available in this step, so I did not register the metadata for these files.

# Design: 8 PBMC CyTOF samples (4 pre, 4 post), 3000 events each. Raw ion counts -> arcsinh(x/5).
# NOTE: metadata patient_id is p1-p4 (pre) and p5-p8 (post): no donor appears twice, so the
# analysis is UNPAIRED (4 vs 4) despite the stated "same four donors" design.
# Choices that read the data: FlowSOM grid 10x10 -> metaclusters k=K; annotation from median lineage
# marker heatmap (CUTS/labels in ANNOT below, set after inspecting output/cluster_medians.csv).
suppressMessages({library(CATALYST);library(diffcyt);library(flowCore);library(SummarizedExperiment);library(limma);library(ggplot2)})
set.seed(1); K <- 10
dir.create("output",FALSE); dir.create("figures",FALSE)
d <- "/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-cytof/"
md <- read.csv(paste0(d,"metadata.csv")); md$condition <- factor(md$condition, levels=c("pre","post"))
panel <- read.csv(paste0(d,"panel.csv"))
fs <- read.flowSet(paste0(d,md$file_name), truncate_max_range=FALSE)
sce <- prepData(fs, panel, md, features=panel$fcs_colname[panel$marker_type!="none"],
  panel_cols=list(channel="fcs_colname",antigen="antigen",class="marker_type"),
  md_cols=list(file="file_name",id="sample_id",factors=c("condition","patient_id")), cofactor=5)
sce <- cluster(sce, features=NULL, xdim=10, ydim=10, maxK=K, seed=1)
# features NULL -> type markers (lineage)
cl <- cluster_ids(sce, paste0("meta",K))
sce$cluster_id <- cl
med <- t(sapply(levels(cl), function(k) rowMedians(assay(sce,"exprs")[rowData(sce)$marker_class=="type", cl==k, drop=FALSE])))
colnames(med) <- rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$marker_class=="type"]
write.csv(cbind(cluster=levels(cl), n_cells=as.vector(table(cl)), med), "output/cluster_medians.csv", row.names=FALSE)
if (!file.exists("output/annotation.csv")) { message("Inspect output/cluster_medians.csv, write output/annotation.csv (cluster,population), rerun"); quit() }
ann <- read.csv("output/annotation.csv")
sce$population <- factor(ann$population[match(as.character(cl), ann$cluster)])
# proportions
tab <- table(sce$sample_id, sce$population)
prop <- prop.table(tab,1)*100
long <- as.data.frame(as.table(prop)); names(long) <- c("sample_id","population","percent")
long <- merge(long, md, by="sample_id"); write.csv(long,"output/population_frequencies_per_sample.csv",row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame.matrix(tab),"output/population_counts_per_sample.csv")
# DA: edgeR on populations (unpaired, 4 vs 4), BH
sce$cluster_id <- sce$population
ei <- data.frame(sample_id=md$sample_id, condition=md$condition, patient_id=md$patient_id)
sce2 <- sce; metadata(sce2)$experiment_info <- ei
dc <- calcCounts(sce2)
design <- createDesignMatrix(ei, cols_design="condition"); contrast <- createContrast(c(0,1))
res <- testDA_edgeR(dc, design, contrast, min_cells=3, min_samples=2)
tt <- as.data.frame(rowData(res)); 
sm <- aggregate(percent~population+condition, long, mean); sw <- reshape(sm, idvar="population", timevar="condition", direction="wide")
out <- merge(tt, sw, by.x="cluster_id", by.y="population")
out$log2_ratio_post_vs_pre <- log2(out$percent.post/out$percent.pre)
names(out)[names(out)=="p_val"] <- "pvalue"; names(out)[names(out)=="p_adj"] <- "adjusted_pvalue"
names(out)[names(out)=="percent.pre"] <- "mean_percent_pre"; names(out)[names(out)=="percent.post"] <- "mean_percent_post"
write.csv(out,"output/differential_abundance.csv",row.names=FALSE)
# Wilcoxon-free sanity: per-population Welch t on logit proportions
# figures
p <- ggplot(long, aes(condition, percent, colour=condition)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape=NA) + geom_point(position=position_jitter(.1)) +
  facet_wrap(~population, scales="free_y") + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position="none")
ggsave("figures/population_frequencies.png",p,width=11,height=8,dpi=300); ggsave("figures/population_frequencies.pdf",p,width=11,height=8)
png("figures/lineage_heatmap.png",1800,1200,res=200); print(plotExprHeatmap(sce, features=rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$marker_class=="type"], by="cluster_id", k=NULL, scale="last", bars=TRUE, perc=TRUE)); dev.off()
# DS (functional markers) per population
dm <- calcMedians(sce2)
rs <- testDS_limma(dc, dm, design, contrast, min_cells=3, min_samples=2)
write.csv(as.data.frame(rowData(rs)),"output/differential_state.csv",row.names=FALSE)

import pandas as pd
d=pd.read_csv('output/cluster_medians.csv')
def f(r):
    if r.n_cells<100: return 'Rare/ambiguous (<100 cells total)'
    p=lambda m:r[m]>1.5
    if p('CD3'): return 'CD4 T cells' if p('CD4') else 'CD8 T cells'

    if p('CD14'): return 'CD14+ monocytes'
    if p('CD16') and p('CD56'): return 'NK cells'

results.text:
Recode the marker classes.
**Result:** I found five main populations. After vaccination, CD14+ monocytes rose from 19.6% to 30.1% of cells. Every lymphoid population fell by a similar relative amount. No functional-marker changes survived correction.

**Caveats**
- **Not paired:** the stated design is four donors sampled before and after. But `metadata.csv` gives p1–p4 for the pre samples and p5–p8 for the post samples. No donor appears twice, so I ran an unpaired 4 vs 4 comparison. If the donors really are shared, a paired model would be stronger. That needs a corrected donor mapping.
- **Fall in lymphoid cells is probably an artefact:** frequencies sum to 100%, so a monocyte increase pushes the other populations down. The lymphoid drops are relative, not evidence that those cells were lost. I can't tell this from a true loss without absolute counts. The edgeR TMM normalization only partly corrects for this.
- **P-values are very small:** the sample-to-sample variation is unusually tight, so the p-values look extreme (down to 8.5e-14 for monocytes). Treat the direction and size of the change as the finding. With four samples per group, the exact p-values are not reliable.
- **Clusters and labels are mine:** I clustered on the lineage markers only (FlowSOM, 10 metaclusters) and assigned labels by hand from the median marker levels in `output/cluster_medians.csv`. The labels follow canonical marker rules. The cluster I called "CD16+ monocytes/neutrophil-like" became the CD14+ monocyte group after the final rerun, so check that label.

**Populations** (5,963 CD14+ monocyte cells, 4,509 CD8, 6,688 CD4, 3,380 B, 3,426 NK, plus 34 rare cells in four tiny clusters, from `output/cluster_medians.csv`)

| Population | Defining markers |
|---|---|
| CD4 T cells | CD45+ CD3+ CD4+ |
| CD8 T cells | CD45+ CD3+ CD8a+ |
| B cells | CD45+ CD19+ |
| NK cells | CD45+ CD16+ CD56+, CD3− |
| CD14+ monocytes | CD45+ CD14+ |
| Rare/ambiguous | Four clusters of 1–23 cells in total, left unassigned |

**Frequency comparison** (mean % of cells, 4 samples per group; `output/differential_abundance.csv`)

| Population | Pre | Post | log2 ratio (post/pre) | Adjusted p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CD14+ monocytes | 19.6 | 30.1 | +0.62 | 5e-13 |
| CD4 T cells | 30.0 | 25.7 | −0.22 | 4e-6 |
| CD8 T cells | 20.0 | 17.6 | −0.18 | 1.3e-5 |
| B cells | 15.0 | 13.2 | −0.19 | 3e-6 |
| NK cells | 15.3 | 13.2 | −0.21 | 9e-7 |
| Rare (34 cells) | 0.11 | 0.18 | +0.69 | 0.18 (not significant) |

**Functional markers:** I compared pSTAT1, pSTAT3, Ki-67, pERK and Granzyme B within each population. Nothing was significant after correction (smallest adjusted p was 0.33, for monocyte Ki-67 and the rare group's Granzyme B). The test is `output/differential_state.csv`, a per-sample median t-test. The comparison has little power with four samples per group.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1`:
- scripts/analysis.R
- output/differential_abundance.csv
- output/differential_state.csv
- output/population_frequencies_per_sample.csv
- output/population_counts_per_sample.csv
- output/cluster_medians.csv
- output/annotation.csv
- figures/population_frequencies.png
- figures/population_frequencies.pdf

The lineage heatmap is not produced: the plotting call failed and I removed it.

# Design: one row per patient (n=120); outcome OS (months), event = 1 - censored (censored=1 means alive).
# Model: Cox PH, stage as categorical (reference I) + age (continuous, per year). No data-driven choices.
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from lifelines import CoxPHFitter
from lifelines.statistics import proportional_hazard_test, multivariate_logrank_test
d = pd.read_csv('/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-clin/clinical.csv')
d['event'] = 1 - d['censored']
X = pd.get_dummies(d['stage'], prefix='stage', drop_first=True).astype(float)
m = pd.concat([d[['os_months', 'event', 'age']], X], axis=1)
cph = CoxPHFitter().fit(m, 'os_months', 'event')
s = cph.summary
out = pd.DataFrame({'term': s.index, 'hazard_ratio': s['exp(coef)'].values,
    'ci_lower_95': s['exp(coef) lower 95%'].values, 'ci_upper_95': s['exp(coef) upper 95%'].values,
    'p_value': s['p'].values})
out['term'] = out['term'].str.replace('stage_', 'stage ') + out['term'].map(lambda t: ' vs I' if t.startswith('stage_') else ' (per year)')
out.to_csv('output/cox_stage_age_hazard_ratios.csv', index=False)
# global stage test: LRT vs age-only model
a = CoxPHFitter().fit(m[['os_months', 'event', 'age']], 'os_months', 'event')
lr = 2 * (cph.log_likelihood_ - a.log_likelihood_)
from scipy.stats import chi2
p = chi2.sf(lr, 3)
ph = proportional_hazard_test(cph, m, time_transform='rank').summary
ph.to_csv('output/ph_test.csv')
with open('output/model_notes.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(f"n={len(d)}, events={d.event.sum()}\nLRT stage (3 df) chi2={lr:.2f}, p={p:.3g}\nconcordance={cph.concordance_index_:.3f}\n")
    f.write(d.groupby('stage').agg(n=('event', 'size'), events=('event', 'sum'), median_os=('os_months', 'median')).to_string())
print(out.to_string()); print(open('output/model_notes.txt').read()); print(ph)

results.text:
Censored=1 means alive, so event = 1 − censored.
The result is odd: older age is strongly protective, and stage IV looks protective. I'll check whether age and stage are confounded.
Stage does not show a clear association with overall survival in the way you'd expect. The age-adjusted result is a statistical artifact of how age relates to survival in this data, so I wouldn't read it as biology.

**Cox model (n=120, 64 deaths).** The model uses stage (reference I) plus age per year. The hazard ratios are in `output/cox_stage_age_hazard_ratios.csv`.

| Term | HR | 95% CI | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stage II vs I | 0.93 | 0.46–1.88 | 0.83 |
| Stage III vs I | 1.00 | 0.51–1.99 | 0.99 |
| Stage IV vs I | 0.22 | 0.085–0.55 | 0.0013 |
| Age (per year) | 0.84 | 0.81–0.88 | 2×10⁻¹⁷ |

- **Stage IV:** the model gives a protective hazard ratio, which is clinically implausible.
- **Overall stage test:** the likelihood-ratio test for stage (3 df) gives p = 0.001, but only because of the stage IV term.
- **Age:** it is strongly protective, with each extra year cutting the hazard by about 16%.
- **Why I distrust this:**
  - Age and survival time correlate at r = 0.95 (`output/confounding_check.txt`). Age is almost a proxy for survival time, which looks like a data-generation or coding feature rather than a real effect.
  - Survival is nearly identical across stages: median OS is 41.7–44.2 months and deaths are 15–17 per group.
  - Without age in the model, no stage differs from stage I (HR 0.92, 1.10 and 0.95; all p > 0.78).
  - Age and stage are roughly balanced, so age is not confounding stage in the usual sense. Adding age is what produces the stage IV result.
  - The proportional-hazards test fails for age (p = 2×10⁻⁹), so the age effect is not constant over time. The stage terms pass it.
- **Conclusion:** the unadjusted data show no stage–survival association, and the age-adjusted stage IV effect should not be interpreted clinically. Check how age was recorded before relying on this. For example, it may have been derived from follow-up.
- **Data coding:** I used event = 1 − `censored`, because the data dictionary says `censored` = 1 means the patient was alive at last follow-up.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1`:
- `output/cox_stage_age_hazard_ratios.csv`
- `output/ph_test.csv`
- `output/model_notes.txt`
- `output/confounding_check.txt`
- `scripts/cox_stage.py`
- `scripts/check_confounding.py`

results.text:
Note that censored=1 means alive, so event = 1 - censored.
The result is odd: age is strongly protective and stage IV looks protective. I'll check whether age and stage are confounded.
**Stage is not associated with overall survival on its own. Stage IV looks protective only after adjusting for age, and I don't trust that result.**

The model is a Cox proportional hazards fit on 120 patients, with stage as a categorical term (reference stage I) and age as a continuous covariate. The event is death, coded as 1 − `censored`, because `censored = 1` means the patient was alive at last follow-up (per the data dictionary). Each stage has 30 patients and 15–17 deaths.

| Term | HR | 95% CI | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stage II vs I | 0.93 | 0.46–1.88 | 0.83 |
| Stage III vs I | 1.00 | 0.51–1.99 | 0.99 |
| Stage IV vs I | 0.22 | 0.09–0.55 | 0.001 |
| Age (per year) | 0.84 | 0.81–0.88 | <0.001 |

- **Joint test:** the likelihood-ratio test for stage against an age-only model gives χ² = 16.2 on 3 degrees of freedom, p = 0.001. This comes entirely from stage IV.
- **Unadjusted model:** without age, no stage differs from stage I (HR 0.92, 1.10 and 0.95 for stages II–IV, p ≥ 0.78). Median OS is about 42–44 months in every stage (`output/stage_only_unadjusted_hr.csv`).
- **Why stage IV looks protective:** age is almost the same across stages (mean 59–61 years). The adjusted stage IV effect therefore doesn't come from age being unevenly spread between stages.
- **Age effect is implausible:** it is strongly protective (HR 0.84 per year), and age correlates with OS at Spearman 0.95. Older age predicting longer survival is the opposite of the usual direction. The concordance of 0.93 is very high for clinical data. I suspect a data-coding problem, such as age or `os_months` being derived from one another, or a simulated dataset. Please check the origin of these columns before using the stage IV estimate.
- **Proportional hazards:** the Schoenfeld-residual test fails for age (p = 2×10⁻⁹) and passes for the stage terms (p ≥ 0.78). The age HR is therefore an average over a time-varying effect.
- **Limits:** the CIs are wide because there are about 16 events per stage. I ran no multiplicity correction, since the question is a single model.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1`:
- `scripts/cox_stage.py`
- `scripts/check_confounding.py`
- `output/cox_stage_age_hazard_ratios.csv`
- `output/stage_joint_test.csv`
- `output/ph_assumption_test.csv`
- `output/stage_only_unadjusted_hr.csv`
